# MovieVolume <img class="product" src="media/bl-20x14.png" alt="BlitzLLVM" title="BlitzLLVM" width="20" height="14">

<div align="center">

[Command Index](Command-Index) · [BlitzBasic](BlitzBasic) · [Movies](BlitzBasic-Movies)

</div>


```blitzbasic
MovieVolume:Void movie:Int32, volume:Float32
```

| Parameter | Mode | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `movie` | In | Int32 | required | A movie handle from [OpenMovie](OpenMovie). |
| `volume` | In | Float32 | required | The volume from 0 to 1. |

## Description

<img class="product" src="media/bl-20x14.png" alt="BlitzLLVM" title="BlitzLLVM" width="20" height="14"> This command does not exist in the original Blitz products. BlitzLLVM adds it.

Sets the volume of the sound of a movie, from 0 (silent) to 1 (the sound of the file, which is also the volume of a new movie). Values outside of that are brought to the nearest of the two. The volume stays when the movie is paused, stopped or sought. The picture is not affected. This is a BlitzLLVM extension: the originals play a movie at the volume of the file.

## Differences

* The sound of a movie plays on a channel of its own ([MovieChannel](MovieChannel)), so [ChannelVolume](ChannelVolume) on it sets the same volume, and the volume of its [audio bus](Audio-Buses) applies on top.
* A debug build (`-d`) stops the program when the movie does not exist, for example the 0 of a movie that failed to open, other builds ignore the command, see [Debug handle checks](Debug-Handle-Checks).

## Examples

```blitzbasic
MovieVolume movie, 0.5   ; half as loud
```
